solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insisting on protocol, Queen blocks movement in street

indicators.note: the whole of the movement with the Queen inside sits within the street abbreviation
the Queen blocks the movement by standing in the middle of it

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching movement
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A stickler for etiquette notes the monarch stopping a procession in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' suggests a parade, but here it is an involuntary twitch; R is the Queen, from Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strict demands that rules and correct procedure be followed exactly.

clue.text: Back among the losers?

definitions.meaning: to back a proposal is to support it formally
coming next after the winner puts you at the head of those who lost

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they've slipped behind into the beaten pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to support it; the runner-up finishes first of the beaten field.

clue.text: Theatre individuals repeatedly interrupted by singular replies

indicators.note: interrupted by means the theatre word is broken by the singular letter

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: repeatedly says the same singular letter breaks into the individuals as well

parts.note: individuals are single ones

explanation.surface: Actors keep being cut off by a lone voice answering back.
explanation.walkthrough: S breaks into REP to give RESP and, 'repeatedly', into ONES to give ONSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses are answers given to questions or remarks.

clue.text: Knockout volume about hospital suppressed by revolutionary Russian writer

indicators.note: in a down answer, being suppressed by means sitting underneath, so the revolutionary comes first

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: about means the knockout and volume letters go around the hospital letter

parts.note: H is the map symbol for a hospital

explanation.surface: A revolutionary keeps down a stunning book on a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H inside KOV to give KHOV; 'suppressed by' sets CHE above it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was a Russian playwright and short-story writer.

clue.text: Account and targeted article backing educational establishment

indicators.note: backing means the words targeted and article are read from right to left

parts.note: to have targeted something is to have aimed at it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A financial account and a pointed piece of writing supporting a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the pair round together to give ADEMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship, the collective higher-education establishment.

clue.text: Inclination to discontinue treatment, ultimately

parts.note: to can something is to stop it, as in 'can it'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of treatment

explanation.surface: A tendency to stop treatment in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cant is a slope or tilt, an incline away from the vertical.

clue.text: No girl recalled Germany as brilliant

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the words no and girl are read backwards

parts.note: a maid is a girl
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A girl remembers Germany as a dazzling place.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant is a diamond cut with many facets to maximise its sparkle.

clue.text: I'm upset over Mike, an impressionist

indicators.note: over in a down answer means placed above the next piece
upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads upwards

parts.note: mike is short for microphone, also spelt mic

explanation.surface: A comic says they're upset about a microphone, as impressionists do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IM into MI, set above MIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic copies other people's voices and mannerisms, which is what an impressionist does.

clue.text: Writer on the move in Ardennes?

indicators.note: on the move suggests the letters of Ardennes shift into a new order

explanation.surface: An author travelling through the wooded Ardennes region.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was the Danish writer of fairy tales.

clue.text: Nut tree ready? Cut, then chop

indicators.note: then sets the chopping word straight after the shortened money word
cut here means the word for ready money loses its final letter

parts.note: ready, or readies, is slang for cash
to hew is to chop with an axe

explanation.surface: A grower asks whether a nut tree is ready for felling, then chopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims CASH to CAS; 'then' just joins it to HEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a tropical tree grown for its kidney-shaped nuts.

clue.text: Nothing by my side, ultimately affected — thus?

definitions.text: Nothing by my side, ultimately affected — thus?

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
something by my side is near me

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word affected

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost a limb laments having nothing at their side.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a person with nothing at one side, so affected, has a single arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Having only one arm means there is nothing hanging at one side of the body.

clue.text: One, possibly probationary (they will need development)

definitions.text: One, possibly probationary (they will need development)

indicators.note: letters that need developing are to be worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: P marks a probationary driver, as on Australian P-plates

explanation.surface: A probationer, along with others like them, still has a lot of growing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ONE, P and THEY are rearranged; read whole, the clue describes a beginner on probation who still needs developing.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a novice or new convert, someone still on trial and learning.

clue.text: Carrying drink, Carol loses head

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter of the word for carol is dropped

parts.note: to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: A carol singer holding a drink goes off their head.
explanation.definitionFit: To be toting something is to be carrying it, often a weapon or bag.

clue.text: To express agreement is not for a scoundrel

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: Siding with a villain is no way to signal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to agree with someone or say that you share their view.

clue.text: Allocate a second feature of horoscope

parts.note: each horoscope is organised under a star sign

explanation.surface: An astrologer hands out a second star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign something is to allot or give it to someone.

clue.text: Retuned TV unassisted, restricting onset of certain irregular movements

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hem in the single letter from the next word
retuned suggests the letters are adjusted into another order
onset of means the opening letter of the word certain

explanation.surface: Someone retunes the television without help, apart from fiddling at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retuned' rearranges TVUNASSISTED; 'restricting' puts C (first of 'certain') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: St Vitus's dance is the old name for Sydenham's chorea, a disorder causing jerky involuntary movements.

clue.text: Italian cardinal's expression of ego?

parts.note: a cardinal number in Italian names the top spot, and calling yourself that is a boast; it looks like a churchman

explanation.surface: A boastful prince of the Roman church shows off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman but means a counting number, the Italian for 'first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'number one', used in English to mean oneself or the best.

clue.text: Certainly from Carnoustie?

definitions.meaning: something from Carnoustie comes from a famous golf links

explanation.surface: Someone confirms they hail from a Scottish golfing town.
explanation.walkthrough: CARNOUSTIE is a championship golf course on the east coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'naturally, yes'; anything from Carnoustie also comes from a golf course.

clue.text: Endless vice of this man, I fancy, would be clothes

definitions.text: Endless vice of this man, I fancy, would be clothes

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at an imaginative rearrangement of the letters
endless means the last letter of vice is dropped

explanation.surface: A man whose endless failing is that he would be nothing but his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves VIC; 'fancy' rearranges VIC with OFTHISMANI. Read whole, the clue describes someone whose vice makes them their wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion victim slavishly follows trends, so that their clothes seem to define them.

clue.text: Opposite — to prose?

definitions.meaning: the opposite or reverse of something
the alternative to writing in prose is writing in poetry

explanation.surface: A question of whether something is contrary to prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means reversed or contrary; split in two, it describes writing in poetic lines rather than prose.

clue.text: Expression in second of dictionaries — it means 'ends'

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

indicators.note: second of means the second letter of dictionaries is taken

explanation.surface: A lexicographer explains what a word in the second volume of dictionaries means.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end points, such as the last stations on railway lines.

clue.text: Bill Parry receives degree

indicators.note: receives means the parry word takes the degree letter inside

parts.note: to parry a blow is to avert it

explanation.surface: A man called Parry is awarded a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'Parry' look like a person's name; Bill is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice or poster, a form of advertisement.

clue.text: Zero-tax company turned over in paper?

indicators.note: turned over means the three pieces are read from the back

parts.note: zero is the figure O
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A tax-free firm overturned in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a book or paper size made by folding a sheet into eight leaves.

clue.text: Well-oiled hose getting cut

indicators.note: getting cut means the last letter of the hosiery word is lopped off

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights

explanation.surface: A well-lubricated hosepipe gets chopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-oiled is slang for drunk, as is tight.

clue.text: Find mutant absorbing uncommon radiation

indicators.note: absorbing means the shuffled letters take another word inside them
mutant suggests the letters of find change form

parts.note: something uncommon is rare

explanation.surface: A scientist discovers a mutant that soaks up unusual radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutant' rearranges the letters of 'Find' to INFD.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared is electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths just longer than visible red light.

clue.text: Opening you wouldn't make a dash for?

definitions.meaning: an entrance to a mine tunnel

definitions.text: you wouldn't make a dash for?
definitions.meaning: in Morse code the short signal, the dot, is spoken as dit, the opposite of a dash

explanation.surface: A gap that isn't worth running to.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A DIT, it is the Morse dot rather than a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal entrance or passage into a mine.

clue.text: Fashion business newspaper rated 'collapsing'

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

indicators.note: collapsing suggests the word rated falls apart and reforms

explanation.surface: A tabloid's ratings of the fashion industry fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal name for the clothing industry.

clue.text: One's crazy to interrupt this writer for a short time

indicators.note: to interrupt means the pieces break into the middle of the word for the writer

parts.note: the setter calls themself this writer, giving me
one is I, the roman numeral; the 's is just 'is'
a crazy person is a nut

explanation.surface: It's mad to interrupt someone while they are writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is sixty seconds, so 'just a minute' means a brief moment.

clue.text: Heart but not head starts to accede to your plea

indicators.note: but not head means the word for heart loses its first letter

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

indicators.note: starts to points to the opening letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A heartfelt request, without a leader, asking you to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not head' trims CENTRE to ENTRE; 'starts to' takes A, T, Y from 'accede to your'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or appeal.

clue.text: Stuff I leave in place

indicators.note: in means the two pieces sit inside the word for place

parts.note: to place something is to put it
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Someone says they'll put down their things and go.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff yourself is to eat greedily, which is the idiom 'pig out'.
